text: But there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you. They will smuggle in destructive heresies, denying the Master who bought them, and so bring swift destruction on themselves.
Many will follow their debauchery, and because of them the way of truth will be slandered.
In their greed they will exploit you with fabricated words. Their condemnation, pronounced long ago, is not idle, and their destruction is not asleep.

versions.text: In their greed they will exploit you with fabricated words. Their condemnation has long been ready, and their destruction is not asleep.
versions.explanation: οὐκ ἀργεῖ means "is not idle / is not lingering," an active image parallel to "is not asleep." "Has long been ready" loses that parallel imagery of the verdict already at work.

text: For if God did not spare the angels when they sinned, but cast them down to hell in chains of darkness, handing them over to be kept for judgment;

versions.text: For if God did not spare the angels when they sinned, but cast them into hell, handing them over to chains of darkness to be kept for judgment;
versions.explanation: In the Greek, the chains of darkness are the means of the casting down (σειραῖς ζόφου ταρταρώσας), not what they were handed over to. A footnote noting that "hell" here translates "Tartarus" would also help readers.

text: and if he did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, a herald of righteousness, with seven others, when he brought the flood upon a world of the ungodly;
and if he condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ruin, reducing them to ashes and making them an example of what is coming to the ungodly;
and if he rescued righteous Lot, worn down by the depraved conduct of the lawless—
for that righteous man, living among them, was tormented in his righteous soul day after day by the lawless deeds he saw and heard—
then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial and to hold the unrighteous for punishment on the day of judgment,
especially those who follow the corrupt cravings of the flesh and despise all authority. Bold and arrogant, they do not tremble to slander glorious beings,
whereas angels, though greater in strength and power, do not bring a slanderous judgment against them.

versions.text: whereas angels, though greater in strength and power, do not bring a slanderous judgment against them before the Lord.
versions.explanation: The phrase "before the Lord" (παρὰ κυρίῳ) is not present in the base text used here; it is an addition from a variant reading. If retained, it should be marked in a footnote rather than in the text.

text: These men are like irrational animals, creatures of instinct born to be caught and killed. They slander what they do not understand, and like animals they too will be destroyed,
suffering the wrong they have earned as their wages. They count it a pleasure to carouse in broad daylight. They are stains and blemishes, reveling in their deceptions while they feast with you,
their eyes full of adultery, insatiable for sin. They lure unstable souls; their hearts are trained in greed; they are children of a curse.
They have left the straight road and gone astray, following the way of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the wages of wickedness.
But he was rebuked for his transgression: a mute donkey spoke with a human voice and restrained the prophet's madness.
These men are springs without water, mists driven by a storm; the gloom of darkness is reserved for them.
For they mouth high-sounding but empty words, and by appealing to the lusts of the flesh and to debauchery they lure those who are barely escaping from those who live in error.

versions.text: For with high-sounding but empty words they appeal to the lusts of the flesh and to debauchery, luring those who have barely escaped from those who live in error.
versions.explanation: The Greek has a single main verb (δελεάζουσιν, "they entice"), but the current rendering uses two verbal ideas ("appeal to" and "luring"), which blurs the structure. Also, ἀποφεύγοντας is a present participle ("are barely escaping"), describing people still in the process of getting free, which fits the danger being described.

text: They promise them freedom while they themselves are slaves of corruption—for a person is a slave to whatever has mastered him.

For if they have escaped the defilements of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and are then entangled and overcome by them again, they are worse off at the end than they were at the beginning.

versions.text: For if they have escaped the defilements of the world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and are then entangled and overcome by them again, they are worse off at the end than they were at the beginning.
versions.explanation: The base text reads "the Lord and Savior" without the possessive "our" (ἡμῶν is a variant reading). Better to follow the base text or note the variant.

text: It would have been better for them never to have known the way of righteousness than, having known it, to turn away from the holy commandment entrusted to them.
What the true proverb says has happened to them: "A dog returns to its own vomit," and, "A washed sow goes back to wallowing in the mud."
